utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were you aware, General Novakovic, that General Perisic contemplated criminal and disciplinary proceedings to be taken against you and against Generals Celeketic, Bjelanovic, and Mrksic for the responsibility that he asserted you had in the fall of the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon. At one point he told us that when he informed us of the decision of the Supreme Council on our retirement. I immediately commented on that by saying that that would have been the most beneficial solution for all three of us, but if they were to try us that would be a trial against the Army of Yugoslavia primarily. And this is what he should count on, and that for us the best way to establish the truth about what had happened would be to have that trial take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What was it precisely that General Perisic informed you about in respect of proceedings, criminal or disciplinary proceedings?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a note for interpreters. He uttered just one sentence, namely, that there was a possibility for that. He did not expand on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I see. So he said there was a possibility of what? I'd like you to try to recall because -- to the best of your recollection precisely the words he used.

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That there was a possibility that a court would look into our responsibility. That's the sentence I remember because it was of great importance for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, who was -- sir, who was Colonel Bulat?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The late Colonel Bulat, his first name was Cedomir, was commander of the 21st Kordun Corps. He was removed from that post subsequently. When on Saturday, the 5th of August, 1995, I returned from Geneva and found a dispatch of General Mrksic appointing me deputy commander of the Serbian Army for Kordun and Banija, commanders of brigades of the Kordun Corps requested that Colonel Bulat be appointed corps commander so that they -- because they, soldiers and the people, had more faith in him than the then-commander, Colonel Bosanac. I accepted that, and from the 5th of August until the end Colonel Bulat was the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we have Prosecution Exhibit 2202 on the monitor, and I'm interested in e-court English translation 06187763 ET, page 1; and B/C/S page 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Sir -- and this is a text taken from the collegium of the General Staff dated the 30th of October, 1995. And you will see a portion of -- I want to direct your attention to the portion that deals with Risto Matovic, the second entry for Risto Matovic. There are two paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And I direct Your Honours' attention as well to the second entry for Risto Matovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Sir, have you had a chance to read that text?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I have the chance to read what it says here, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Having read that text, sir, first of all, can you tell us who General Risto Matovic is?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what -- which duty he held in the General Staff, maybe for mobilisation call-up -- well, one of the top brass within the General Staff, but I don't know his precise duty or post.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, this text reads: "In the sector we have launched an investigation against Bulat and it is completed. Five witnesses and suspects were interviewed. The committee with General Ristic at the helm proposes to institute proceedings against him to inculpate him and to punish him. We have the complete material now." Were you aware that the VJ had launched an investigation against Colonel Bulat?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What -- when did you become aware that the VJ had launched an investigation against Colonel Bulat?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Colonel Bulat himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And when was that? When did you learn that, in 1995, 1996, 1997?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was immediately in 1995. It seems to me to be so, Mr. Harmon. I cannot be too precise about that, but I believe it was still 1995 or maybe the beginning of 1996. Of course after August 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And Colonel Bulat was being investigated for what reason?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, I think it went for military disciplinary courts and tribunals which existed in the army at the time which tried disciplinary infractions and had certain jurisdiction over certain matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And for what reason was he being --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to be more precise. I think it's important when it comes to the use of the term. Mr. Harmon mentions investigation and here it is stated "examination" or "inquiry." I think those -- this distinction is important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where does it say "inquiry," Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm reading the B/C/S version, the second paragraph of Mr. Matovic's intervention. It is stated here: "In the sector we instituted inquiries against Bulat..." et cetera. As you see in English, the term is followed by a question mark and it says "investigation" question mark. And the interpreters in the booth in my opinion correctly translated that very specific legal term with a very important legal distinction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Interpreter, are you saying -- when you say the interpreters in the booth in my opinion, are you telling us your opinion or you are translating?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm interpreting Mr. Lukic's words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Anyway, Mr. Lukic, I -- in the translation that we have before us we don't have a question mark after "investigation." We've got a question mark before "an," after "launched" and a slash. I am prepared to accept that you are saying that somebody is querying the interpretation there or the translation there. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I asked the witness if he was aware if there was an investigation opened against Colonel Bulat, and he answered affirmatively. So I think that resolves the issue, not the issue of whether the text is right but the issue of whether the fact is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, sir, I had asked you before the intervention by my colleague

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And Colonel Bulat was being investigated for what reason? Why was he being investigated?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A disciplinary inquiry and not investigation against Colonel Bulat, my mistake. I failed to notice that - was initiated because of the surrender of the 21st Kordun Corps to the Croatian Army at the time while he was corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. So this was a disciplinary inquiry being conducted by the VJ for Colonel Bulat's actions in surrendering the 21st Corps of the SVK to the Croatian army; do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is evident from this document, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So I take it the answer is I did understand you correctly and that's the reason why he was being -- there was a disciplinary inquiry?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This disciplinary inquiry did take place. It's stated here that I was interviewed. I remember that correctly. And -- but he -- no disciplinary sanction was meted out to Colonel Bulat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was Colonel Bulat brought before a disciplinary -- a VJ disciplinary inquiry panel and questioned himself?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't know that, Mr. Harmon. What I do know is that I gave my statement to General Ristic in the presence of that general and Mr. Bulat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. So, General, how was it that you were -- what were the circumstances under which you gave a statement to General Ristic? Were you summoned to appear before General Ristic at a certain date and a time?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Harmon. First Colonel Bulat came to me to ask me to provide a statement during that inquiry. After that, he arranged with the gentleman who was in charge of that inquiry, and it's stated here that this was Mr. Ristic, for me to get somewhere at a certain date -- on a certain date at a certain time. There was no official summons or writ, and I just came there and told them what I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, the recommendation of General Ristic was that proceedings be instituted against Colonel Bulat. Were they ever instituted? Were any sanctions ever imposed against Colonel Bulat for giving up the 21st Corps to the Croatian Army?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the witness answered this question on page 50, line 5.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Page 51, line 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I asked the question if there were any sanctions. That's a broader question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, at page 51, line 5, it says: "I remember that correctly. And -- but he" -- sorry, my page is running away, "but he - no disciplinary sanction was meted out to Colonel Bulat." So you're saying you're asking about sanctions. He's talking about sanctions there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Disciplinary sanctions. I'm asking if there were any sanctions imposed against him and the question is different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Sir, you can answer -- with the Court's permission you can answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, what I stated, that he did not receive any sanction, I state that on the basis of the following. Colonel Bulat, who was a close friend of mine, never told me that any disciplinary measures had been meted out in connection with these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's 12.00 and this would be an appropriate time to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: General, I want to focus your attention on the documents that you were provided that resulted in your retroactive retirement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could first of all have P1912 on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this document as being the presidential decree of President Lilic retroactively retiring you from professional military service, and it's dated the 22nd of December, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do believe I have an original of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we know that this date of the 22nd of December, 1994, as being the date of the decree is false; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is not, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, the decree -- this decree was not promulgated on the 22nd of December, 1994, because you were still in service in the SVK until I think you told us the 17th of October, 1995. You were still actively serving in the military. So do you accept, General Novakovic, that the date of this decree was not in fact the 22nd of December, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of the time when I was told about it and the time during which I was treated from the date on this document until the 17th of October, 1995, I do believe that this document was not created on that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, I want to direct your attention, sir, to the last paragraph in English, and it is the second paragraph under the reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And if we could scroll up in the English version so we can see. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm directing your attention to the paragraph that reads: "In view of the above it was concluded that there are grounds for the professional military service of the above-named person to be terminated pursuant to Article 107, paragraph 2, of the Law on the Yugoslav Army." Now, this morning you testified - and I'm referring to your testimony at page 21, lines 22 to 25, and I want to clarify this point - your testimony in response to a question from Mr. Lukic was that: "The date of retirement," this is what General Perisic allegedly told you, that: "The date of the retirement had to be what it was because in late 1994 Article 107 of the Law on the Army became invalid and that article enabled servicemen to retire based on their years of service and their age." Is that what General Perisic told you?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood it to be -- that the needs for this date to be determined so stemmed from that circumstance. I cannot claim that Mr. Perisic told me. What I can say that Mr. Perisic or somebody else told me, that this would be the legal basis for my retirement to be regulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So really, General Novakovic, I'm just focusing on the word "invalid" that appears in the text of the transcript today. Were you told that Article 107 became invalid or that it was valid?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was said that the Article 107 was in effect until the 31st of December of the preceding year.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Fine. That clarifies the transcript error that -- that's all I was attempting to do, General Novakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn to P1913 and put that on the monitor, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Sir, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is the decision implementing the presidential decree terminating you retroactively; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And again in this document on its face we can see a number of false statements. One, direct your attention to -- under statement of reasons to the first paragraph where it says this decree was delivered to you on the 25th of December, 1994. That statement is false, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was the decree -- this decree that you have before you delivered to you on the 25th of December, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is written in this decision, that the decree was delivered to me on the 25th of December, 1994, it's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank -- that's what I was asking you. Let's look at the next sentence. The next sentence says on the 30th of December, 1994, you submitted a report stating that you had handed over your duty on that date. Did you submit a report stating that you had handed over your duty on the 30th of December, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you received both the presidential decree, which we looked at before this exhibit, and this decision, you received that -- those copies of those documents when?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime after the 17th of December or maybe on that date or a couple of days afterwards in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, is it December or October? [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for His Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it after the 17th of October or 17th of December?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, October, October. My mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you received copies of those two decisions, did you sign a delivery note?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you backdate the delivery note to reflect the 25th of December, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Why was it, sir, that you backdated the delivery -- the receipt note to December the 25th, 1994? Why didn't you put the correct date when you received those two decisions on the delivery note?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because this was the only way for this whole situation to be resolved and because this was the position as related to me of the -- of both the Supreme Defence Council, president of the republic, president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and chief of the personnel department. It was explained to me that I should place such a date on that document for this document to be valid.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And who told you to place the false date on the document?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The personnel officers who technically drafted those document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You -- by name do you recall who those personnel officers were who drafted these documents?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think chief of personnel administration was General Zoric or a lieutenant-colonel who was involved in drafting those. I know that he graduated from the military academy, but I cannot recall his either first or last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's -- I want to explore with you another topic. The retirement, retroactive retirement, retired you back until -- on the 30th of December, 1994. You were in actual military service until October of 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And as an officer serving through October of 1995, you were entitled to certain benefits, including pension benefits; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we discuss duty, Mr. Harmon, maybe we should be more precise. In actual fact I held a duty in the SVK until the 10th of August, 1995. I held no other duty after that date. And whatever I received was the salary.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So with those dates in mind, let's frame the time-period. From the date of your retroactive retirement, you continued serving a duty in the SVK until the 10th of August, 1995, for which you would have accrued certain pension benefits; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would mean higher pension, maybe a housing issue being resolved, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Sir, I'm trying to focus on one narrow issue here: Your pension benefits. As an acting military -- professional military officer serving in the military, under the VJ you were entitled to receive pension benefits until your service was terminated; correct? I'm sorry that's a bad -- that's a poorly framed question. Let me rephrase the question. General Novakovic, you were entitled -- you were earning pension benefits and rights as long as you were in active military service. That's the normal procedure, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Your active military service you've just told us ended the 10th of August, 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You were retroactively terminated in December of 1994. We know that from the documents. My question, sir, is: Did you and do you receive pension benefits for the time you were in active military service between December of 1994 and the 10th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Frankly speaking, Mr. Harmon, those were minor details for me. What was important for me was to conclude my active military service --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you for a minute. My question was very clear and quite precise. I'll repeat it. Did you and do you receive pension benefits from the time you were in active military service between December of 1994 and the 10th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In reality, yes. But if I was retired as of 30th of December, 1994, if that's what you want to hear, I think that that bit was not calculated into my years of service, did not count for the pension benefits.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I don't understand. You started off by saying "in reality, yes," meaning that yes you do receive pension for the period of the 30th of December, 1994, to August 1995. And now your next sentence is but you think that that bit was not calculated. Surely, if you -- if the answer -- first answer is yes, yes, you do receive it, then it was calculated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in accordance with the laws in force then, had I been retired with the actual factual date when I served in the SVK, then the period between the backdated date of retirement and -- which is the 30th of December, 1994 - and the later date, the 10th of August, 1995, which is when factually my engagement in the SVK was terminated and during which period of time I had status in the VJ, would be calculated as years of service for which pension benefits accrue, as Mr. Harmon says. This is how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So your answer to his question is: Yes, you were -- you are getting pension for that period, 30th of December, 1994, to 10th of August, 1995, that's the short answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it did not get included. Had it been done in accordance with the law, it would have been included; but since this was done with backdating, then obviously it was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you are not receiving it. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me turn now to a different document. If I could have P1914 on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: While we're waiting for P1914 to appear on the monitor, General, can you tell -- is there a reason why you didn't receive the housing benefits to which you were entitled as a general until last year?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I addressed the housing organ in the Belgrade garrison in 1995, they told me that I was not entitled to housing from the army because I was a pensioner. Then I went to the fund for pensioners and I applied to them for housing as a pensioner. Two years later in the fund for pensioners for veterans, they told me that they were not competent to give me housing because I was denied housing in Zagreb as an active officer of the JNA and not as a military pensioner. And they directed me to apply to the housing organ of the VJ in the Belgrade garrison. When I went there they told me that I was not entitled to apply for housing because I had not done it while I was in active duty. It wasn't until General Mrksic and Colonel Bulat intervened and all of us knew that we had all applied for housing while in Krajina, they managed to find the cover of my personnel file which had been sent to Raska garrison, where -- which I never -- where I never was, and I only passed through the town of Raska once in my life. And it wasn't until then that I was allowed to apply for housing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you see on the monitor in front of you, sir, a document. That's a document that bears your signature; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, can you slowly read that document into the record. And I'm only referring to the portion under the word "statement." There's a single sentence. Can you read that into the record, please.

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I hereby state that in accordance with the order of the Chief of the General Staff of the VJ, I accept to be assigned as required by the service in the Army of Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you tell me the circumstances under which you prepared this document?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time General Mrksic, the then-army commander; General Bjelanovic; me; and some other officers were in Banja Luka, in Republika Srpska. General Mrksic at one point in time went to Belgrade. I know he had a problem. He had to go there illegally by crossing the river in a boat. And after that visit he told us that all of us had to write this sort of a statement and all of us did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just understand what you mean by "at that time ... the then-army commander ..." do you mean on the 16th of September, 1995? You have been asking us to be very precise. I want to know whether on the 16th of September, 1995, General Mrksic was a commander; and if so, in which army? Because I think by then the SVK was no longer there, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. It pertains to this very date. As you can see in the heading, it says "Banja Luka," which is in Republika Srpska. We were all together and we considered ourselves the remnants of that army, which in reality no longer existed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. So he was not a commander on that day because the army didn't exist on the 16th of September. Just so that we understand, two years down the line when we read what you wrote here we want to know exactly what you meant by this. Okay. Anyway, I understand now. Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who prepared the text of this document?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I worded this myself, bearing in mind the words of General Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We have to go into private session. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session and may we see that P766, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, we will have to redact, if we could, lines 18 and 19 on page 62. I quoted in part a protected document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May it be, please, so redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: General, if we have -- we're going to have to go to the item 3 of this document in English and in B/C/S, please, page 2 of the English. And I think the portion of the paragraph that I want to cite is on page 2 of the Serbian language as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And I want to direct Your Honours' attention to the second paragraph under item 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And, General Novakovic, I'd like to do the same to you. This paragraph says that: "Prior to passing the enactment, the Chief of the General Staff is tasked with conducting an interview with the above-mentioned persons in order to inform them of the decision of the Supreme Defence Council of their duty to place themselves at the disposal of the 30th Personnel Centre following the termination of their professional military service in the Yugoslav Army." Now, this -- were you ever informed, sir, of your duty to place yourself at the disposal of the 30th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who told you that and when were you told that?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Perisic told me that when informing me of the decision on retirement. I think it was then that I had to sign a statement to that effect. The 30th Personnel Centre kept records for the persons in the VRS, but on the 16th of September, which is the date of this document, I still knew nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. If you were not a member of the VJ, what duty did you have to place yourself at the disposal of the 30th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, I would kindly ask you to put specific questions to me so that I can give you specific answers. Whether a member of the Army of Yugoslavia to you means the same as a person with the status within the VJ, when asking me whether I was a member of the VJ do you think it is the same as having the status in the VJ while at the same time being a member of the SVK in the Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: My question to you, sir, was: If you were not a member of the VJ, what duty did you have to place yourself at the disposal of the 30th Personnel Centre? Can you answer that question, please.

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was retired, it was not clear what duty I had when I was no longer member of the VJ. I think that we're dealing with a political position at this point in time. How could the General Staff of the VJ order me as a pensioner to put myself at the disposal of another army, because I was to be placed at the disposal of the 30th Personnel Centre, and I learned of this information simultaneously with learning about my retirement, by way of the presidential decree, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you put yourself at the disposal of the 30th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did not even occur to me, Mr. Harmon, ever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While Mr. Harmon is still looking at his monitor, can I ask a question. When you did not put yourself at the disposal of the 30th personnel army -- personnel centre, were there any consequences for your not doing so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There weren't, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Nobody tried to punish you or tried to inquire why you don't obey this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In your answer, General Novakovic, you say: "Mr. Perisic," this is at page 64, line 1. "Mr. Perisic told me that," that is the duty to place yourself at the disposal of the 30th Personnel Centre, "when informing me of the decision on retirement." That was your answer. General Perisic told you to place yourself at the disposal. What did you tell General Perisic?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for my duty to place myself at the disposal of the 30th Personnel Centre, I didn't tell him anything in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Sir, when did you have that -- what was the date of that conversation with General Perisic?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on my recollection - and I have repeated it several times - it was on the 17th of October, 1995. However, I don't know whether the presidential decree and the decision were handed to me and whether I was supposed to sign the statement accepting to be placed at the disposal of the 30th Personnel Centre on that same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So you're telling us that at no time did you place yourself at the disposal of the 30th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you ever place yourself at the disposal of the commander of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we have Prosecution Exhibit 177 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you still want to stay in --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And is it one -- two 7s --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Three 7s.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Three 7s. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Three 7s. And could we go into public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we have P1777 e-court English translation 0611-7673 ET 1, B/C/S page 82 on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: General Novakovic, is that your signature at the bottom of this document?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, would you read in the last sentence in that document.

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I also hereby accept to be placed at the disposal of the commander of the Army of Republika Srpska." That's the last sentence, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, when did you write this document and where did you write this document?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently in Belgrade, Mr. Harmon, and I think that it had to be on the 17th of October, not on the 7th, as is stated here. I think that this document was created on the 17th of October, and I think that I repeated twice in the last hour or so that I did sign a document of this nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And this was a document -- was this with General Perisic present or was this a result of a meeting that you had with General Perisic on the 17th of October, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The position of the Supreme Defence Council about us having to be placed at the disposal of the 30th Personnel Centre is something that General Perisic told us then, on the 17th of October. I did not sign this statement before him. I signed it at the same time when I signed the other paperwork, namely, the presidential decree, the decision, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So you signed this document after you met with General Perisic on the 17th of October?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Based on my best recollection, that's how it was, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you -- in October of 1995, did you also return the stamp of the SVK -- a rubber stamp of the SVK to the VJ General Staff?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The stamp of the SVK and the diplomatic passport, I turned that over later and I have a record of that hand-over; I have it in my possession to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And to whom did you turn that over, both the diplomatic passport of the SVK and the rubber stamp of the SVK?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I remember, I turned it over to the General Staff. As for the specific organ, I think it was the personnel administration. I'm not entirely sure. I would need to check the document that I have, but it's at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And, sir, why did you turn over to the General Staff of the VJ the rubber stamp of the SVK?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know whom else I could give it to, Mr. Harmon, and I needed to have an official certificate that I no longer had it in my possession. So the most logical thing for me was to go to the General Staff, to hand it over to them, so that they could put it in the military museum.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And was it your intention to have it put into a military museum?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. That was just a comment I made in passing. I simply wanted to turn it over because I no longer was authorised to have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Didn't you turn it over because it was property of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was by no means the property of the VJ, either the diplomatic passport or the stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much on that particular topic. We're going to turn to another topic, General Novakovic, and the topic we're going to turn to is your assignment to the special police. You testified earlier that -- you said that you -- that an operations group in charge of Banija and Kordun was formed in Belgrade and that you were one of the members of the command of that operative group. That testimony is found at page 12999, line 25. In connection with that testimony, you made the following statement, you said: "This is an operative assignment. It's not an assignment to a duty by establishment." That testimony is found at page 13000, line 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do we have a date for this assignment?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The assignment to the operative group, I understood from the evidence, was pursuant to an order of the SSNO of 27 September 1991. The General can correct me if I'm not correct, but that's my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: But my question to you, General Novakovic, is: Can you explain to us the distinction you're trying to make when you say "this is an operative assignment. It's not an assignment to a duty by establishment." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it wasn't something that would require an establishment rank or established formation. It was just a structure which was being created then, and people I appointed who were available, those who organised that thing thought I was supposed to be in Kordun and in this respect there was no establishment book, there were no establishment ranks. And this is why I expressed myself in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So an assignment by establishment would mean -- would it mean an assignment to a specific location with a specific duty post number? Is that how I'm to understand an assignment by establishment?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In essence, that would be so, Mr. Harmon. But the reality was thus, the order that you have - and I unfortunately cannot see it - was dated on the 27th of September, if I remember it correctly. A brigade of special units of police for Kordun, where I was appointed commander, was established on the 2nd of August, 1995 [as interpreted]. I know this to be a reliable fact. In the presence of the then-chief of the administration for special units of police in Krajina, Mr. -- General Borislav Djukic in the village of Pijesanica [phoen], close to Vrginmost.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yeah, I -- Mr. Cannata has pointed out an error in the transcript, General. It says that you were appointed commander -- I'll just see the still transcript because I can't follow on this thing. The year 1995 has been inserted into your answer. It says: " ... where I was appointed commander -- a brigade of special police units for Kordun, where I was appointed commander, was established on the 2nd of August, 1995." 1995 is not correct. It should be a different year, shouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1992. If I said "1995," I'm mistaken. It is known that it was 1992, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's deal with your unit. You said that in your evidence at -- that you commanded the 80th Brigade of the special police that had about 2.000 members. That testimony is found on 13055, line 12. Would you consider, General Novakovic, that a police force of 2.000 men was a large police force?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, I don't know what interpretation you receive. I hear "special police" in my headset. It was not called special police. It was called special units of police, which indicate their purpose. And my answer to your specific question would be as follows. It was a large formation if you talk about normal security circumstances and conditions. But if you take into account the fact that more than 100 kilometres of the line of conflict which stayed the same after UNPROFOR's arrival with Croatian forces on the other side, that front line had to be observed, manned 24/7, 365 days a year. This would be the minimum to be achieved, and that was the basic purpose of that unit so that that population there would feel safe to a certain extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were there other brigades of special units of police in the RSK beside the 80th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why the interpreter mentions SVK. SVK did not exist at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I said "RSK," sir. Were there other brigades of special units of the police in the RSK beside the 80th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon. I received SVK in the interpretation into Serbian. This was the cause of my confusion. There was a special brigade of police in the area of Dalmatia, then special brigade of police in Lika, special brigade of police in Kordun, special brigade of police in Western Slavonia, and a special brigade of police in the eastern part, apart from the 80th Brigade which existed in Kordun.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What was the total number of special policemen in these units? How many were there?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, Mr. Harmon. General Djukic would be familiar with that piece of information. I've never dealt with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lukic asked you a number of questions about the Vance Plan, and your testimony was that the Vance Plan envisioned that the UNPAs would be demilitarised and the armed forces would be disarmed. That testimony is found at 13043, line 1. Your testimony was that the disarming of the armed formations was done, that's at 13043, line 15. And you testified that UN under-Secretary-General Marrack Goulding said that the Serb side had complied. That's at 13043, lines 12 through 19. You further testified, General Novakovic, that General Nambiar, who was the UNPROFOR commander at the time, "never raised as a problem the questions of whether our side was complying with the requirements of the Vance Plan." That's at 13044, line 16. In fact, General Novakovic, the UNPAs were never demilitarised, were they?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you use as a basis for your claim, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll see that in just a minute, General Novakovic. Now, another fact, General Novakovic, is that these special police forces were really not police forces. They weren't policemen. They were soldiers, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, if I were to follow your logic then I would have drawn a conclusion that in the Serbian Army of Krajina there were no soldiers or were very few because they were peasants. There were neither soldiers nor policemen nor nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So were the members of the 80th Special Police Brigade soldiers or were they policemen? Let's start at that level.

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were members of special, or "posebne," units of police, not those units of police who were intended to maintain law and order, fight crime, and control traffic. Rather, of those units of police within the structure of regular police within the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbian Krajina who were in charge of the most important security task, and that would be to prevent the infiltration and incursion of armed forces from the areas where those Croatian forces were in a war deployment without being controlled by anybody or without being controlled by the UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In fact, General Novakovic, UN officials, including General Nambiar and Marrack Goulding, repeatedly complained that the special police were paramilitary forces, isn't that right, and that their presence was a violation of the Vance Plan?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You can answer that yes or no, sir. I don't want a lengthy explanation. I want to try to conclude this portion of my examination. Is that true or not? Did they repeatedly complain and protest that the special police were paramilitary forces and that their presence was a violation of the Vance Plan?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In contacts with me - and this is something I can testify about as a commander of a local brigade, I cannot expand on this - Mr. Kirudja held such a position in contacts with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 5991 on the monitor, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that a Prosecution document?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is it being used for?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Impeachment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, any comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the purpose of this document is exclusively what Mr. Harmon said, then I do not object to it being shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Harmon. Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, in this document I'd like to have page 2 of the English and page 2 of the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Page 1 you'll see in the caption, this is a further report of the Secretary-General pursuant to the Security Council Resolutions 743 and 762. It is dated the 28th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And I'd like to direct Your Honours' attention to paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And as soon as it comes up in your language, General Novakovic, I will ask you to focus on paragraph 4, please. Okay. If -- this paragraph says: "The first two phases of demilitarisation proceeded well. The Yugoslav People's Army completed its withdrawal from Croatia, with the single but significant exception of the Dubrovnik area and the Territorial Defence forces demobilised, placing their weapons in storage depots under a double-lock system. However, the complete demilitarisation of United Nations protected areas has been delayed by a violation of the United Nations plan, which was referred to in my report of 27 July. This is the creation of new Serb militia forces designated variously as 'Special Police,' 'Border Police,' or 'multi-purpose police brigades,' made up of former members of JNA, Territorial Defence forces, and irregular elements, which may total as many as 16.000 armed men equipped with armoured personnel carriers" --

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. We'll turn to the next page in the Serbian language, please. Okay. Let me then partially carry on where I was: " ... which may total as many as 16.000 armed men, equipped with armoured personnel carriers, mortars, and machine-guns. The authorities of the so-called Republic of Serbia Krajina (hereinafter referred to as 'Knin authorities') claim these are police units. The Force Commander considers that their level of armament and their almost total ignorance of police work show that, in reality, they are paramilitary forces. UNPROFOR has vigorously protested this violation of the" -- and if we could turn to the next page in English, please -- "United Nations plan and has pressed repeatedly for the demilitarisation of those newly created units and for the regular police to be armed only with side-arms, in accordance with the plan." Now, sir, if we could focus your attention on paragraph 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And I'd like to focus the Court's attention on paragraph 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Because this is where reference is made to General Nambiar. If we could go to the second sentence it says: "General Nambiar has repeatedly stressed to the authorities in Belgrade and Knin that it is UNPROFOR that exercises the protection functions of the United Nations protected areas and that the presence of these paramilitary units is contrary to the United Nations plan and has caused the Croatian Army to retain some of its forces at the confrontation line." Now, -- so this document, General, contradicts your earlier evidence that General Nambiar indicated that your side was complying with the Vance Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could turn to paragraph 8 of this document, we're going to see a reference to UN Under-Secretary Marrack Goulding. And I think you have 8 in front of you. And I'm only going to read a couple portions of paragraph 8. Paragraph indicates that: "On the 4th of September, Under-Secretary ... Goulding reached an agreement with the Knin authorities that demobilisation of these forces would be undertaken in accordance with an agreed timetable." And if we go to paragraph 9 we'll need to turn to the next page in the Serbian version of this document so General Novakovic can follow. And paragraph 9, sir, reads: "Despite the passage of the dead-line for the first stage of this process, however, demilitarisation has not begun." So there was an agreement with Under-Secretary-General Goulding that dealt with the demobilisation of these forces. And now let's -- I want to direct your attention to another document, General, which deals --

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Sir, let me just -- sir, just let me finish and I'm going to give you a chance to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could turn to 65 ter 5989. This is also a document that is from the Prosecution's 65 ter list, and it is for purposes of impeachment only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for His Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. What do you want to happen to this one, 5991?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could it be given an exhibit number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is so given an exhibit number. May it please entered.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2919.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we turn then to 5989. I'm interested in quickly looking at the first page which will identify what this document is and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've not expressed myself. Let the record reflect that I do not object to showing the next document for impeachment purposes only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So if we could -- the first page, Your Honours, indicates that this is a further report of the Secretary-General pursuant to Security Council Resolution 743. This is dated the 24th of November, 1992, and if we could turn to paragraph 12 which is on page 3 of the English and on page 4 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We'll now focus on what UN Under-Secretary Marrack Goulding had to say about Serb compliance in the UNPAs. This also references General Nambiar, who was the force commander. So if I can direct your attention, General, to paragraph 12, I can see that you only have -- there we have it. Thank you. It reads: "Despite many interventions at the highest level in Belgrade and/or with the various local authorities by the co-chairman of the Steering Committee of the ICFY, Mr. Vance and Lord Owen, by Under-Secretary-General Goulding, by the Force Commander, and by senior UNPROFOR personnel, no progress has been achieved towards demobilisation of these elements." Now, "these elements," sir, are elements that are referred to in the paragraph above, and I would like to direct your attention to what the reference to is. And I'll start on the -- in the English version six lines down. It will start with the word: "These authorities have replaced the JNA and the TDF with Serb militia forces under various guises comprising former JNA and TDF soldiers as well as irregular elements. They may total 16.000 personnel or more and are equipped with armoured personnel carriers, mortars, machine-guns, and other arms prohibited under the peacekeeping plan. They are sometimes claimed by the Knin authorities to be police, but UNPROFOR does not accept this; they are not trained or equipped as police, nor do they perform police functions. Instead, they are" --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Paragraph 11, Your Honour. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me just -- I'll read the last sentence I intend to read. "Instead, they are often deployed along the borders of the UNPAs and at the edges of the 'pink zones,' serving as a paramilitary force in blatant violation of the plan." So, General, your testimony earlier was that Marrack Goulding never complained about what the Serb side had done and that they had complied, and General Nambiar never raised a question as to what your side -- whether they were complying with the requirements of the Vance Plan. It appears that that's not correct, that's not true. They were very dissatisfied with compliance with the Serb side in particular. They were very distressed by the forces that you commanded and alleged that they weren't police. What do you say, General? Now that you've seen these documents where Marrack Goulding, Lord Owen, Cyrus Vance, Nambiar make rather serious - in fact significant - complaints, what do you say, General, and how do you reconcile your previous testimony with these documents?

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, let me ask you, Mr. Harmon, what was the basis for you claiming that I was chief or at the head of those forces? I was not at the head of them. I headed one brigade which was deployed in Kordun. It seems to me, Mr. Harmon, that it's slightly unfair to heap so many things that I am supposed to respond to, particularly your claim that I was the chief man in the -- of those forces. Let me take matters in turn.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let's be perfectly clear. You were the commander of the 80th Special Police Unit. I assert no more. Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MILE NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my testimony I exclusively spoke from my then-position, commander of the 80th Brigade -- special brigade of police in Kordun. And I said that I on occasion met with General Nambiar and that he never uttered any objections to the level of our demilitarisation. Whether he uttered such objections somewhere else and sometimes else -- the same goes for Mr. Goulding. The only time I could hear of such things was in the press. And now, Mr. Harmon, that you claim that those forces, special units of police, may have been regarded as paramilitary units -- well, I can claim to you that there were no APCs or mortars in my brigade. We had -- we had rifles and light machine-guns. We did -- if we could go to the preceding document, paragraph 2, so that we could reach some truth -- if you could please show me paragraph 2 of the document where you read paragraphs 11 and 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't want to interfere in the cross-examination by Mr. Harmon, but I believe that given that this witness has not seen this document before and since it's a voluminous document, it would be only fair that the witness be given that document and we continue tomorrow. It would be only fair for the witness to familiarise himself with the document if Mr. Harmon seeks some specific answers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not necessary, Mr. Lukic. Whichever way the Court decides, it's fine by me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's past --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's past the time we're to adjourn, so I don't want to continue this at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We can return to the issue that General Novakovic raises in the morning. I would be happy to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Once again, sir, you may not discuss this case with anybody, and least of all with the Defence team. Please come back tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning, same courtroom. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 2nd day of September, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
